name: Mastic / hard gum
lead: Mastic gum is a hard, chewy resin from the mastic tree (Pistacia lentiscus) grown mainly on the Greek island of Chios, and it is marketed alongside harder-than-normal gums such as Turkish falim as a jaw-training gum. Several brands now sell mastic-based jawline gum.
It is used in looksmaxxing circles as a food-based way to work the masseter and encourage a more defined lower face.

paras: Prolonged hard chewing makes the masseter and temporalis work against resistance, which may raise muscle stiffness, endurance and possibly size over time. The resin itself has traditional digestive uses, but any jaw effect comes from the chewing load, not the substance.

No controlled study shows mastic gum sculpts the jawline; small studies cover muscle stiffness and oxygen dynamics, not definition. Heavy chewing is associated with jaw muscle pain, TMJ strain and uneven wear, and larger masseters broaden rather than sharpen the face. Forum users themselves raise TMJ worries, so treat it as an unproven gamble.
